const script = `#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code Stop hook: run the test suite when Claude finishes a turn that
# changed code (src/, tests/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock).
#
# Skipping:
#   - Slow tests are listed (one exact test name per line) in
#     .claude/hooks/slow-tests.txt and passed to the test harness as --skip.
#     Run the full suite yourself with plain \`cargo test\`.
#   - MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1 in the environment Claude Code was started
#     from disables the hook entirely.
#
# Exit 2 with the failure output on stderr makes Claude keep working on it.
set -uo pipefail

input=$(cat)
[[ "\${MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 0

cd "\${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(dirname "$0")/../..}" || exit 0

stamp_dir=target/.claude-hook
mkdir -p "$stamp_dir"
paths=(src tests Cargo.toml Cargo.lock)

# Cheap fingerprint of the code: name, size and mtime of every tracked or
# untracked (non-ignored) file under the code paths.
fingerprint=$(git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- "\${paths[@]}" \\
  | xargs -r -d '\\n' stat -c '%n %s %Y' 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)

# Nothing changed since the last passing run.
[[ -f "$stamp_dir/passed" && "$(cat "$stamp_dir/passed")" == "$fingerprint" ]] && exit 0

# First run on a clean tree: assume the committed code is tested.
if [[ ! -f "$stamp_dir/passed" && -z "$(git status --porcelain -- "\${paths[@]}")" ]]; then
  echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/passed"
  exit 0
fi

# Claude already saw these failures and stopped without changing code: let it
# stop instead of looping.
stop_hook_active=$(jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null)
if [[ "$stop_hook_active" == "true" && -f "$stamp_dir/failed" \\
      && "$(cat "$stamp_dir/failed")" == "$fingerprint" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

skip_args=()
slow_list=.claude/hooks/slow-tests.txt
if [[ -f "$slow_list" ]]; then
  while IFS= read -r name; do
    name=\${name%%#*}; name=\${name//[[:space:]]/}
    [[ -n "$name" ]] && skip_args+=(--skip "$name")
  done < "$slow_list"
fi
[[ \${#skip_args[@]} -gt 0 ]] && skip_args=(--exact "\${skip_args[@]}")

log="$stamp_dir/last-run.log"
if cargo test --quiet -- "\${skip_args[@]}" >"$log" 2>&1; then
  echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/passed"
  rm -f "$stamp_dir/failed"
  exit 0
fi

echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/failed"
{
  echo "Stop hook: \\\`cargo test\\\` failed (slow tests in $slow_list skipped). Fix the failures before finishing. Last 80 lines of $log:"
  tail -n 80 "$log"
} >&2
exit 2
`;
const slow = `# Tests the Stop hook (.claude/hooks/run-tests.sh) skips because they take
# more than ~10 s each in a debug build. One exact test name per line;
# '#' starts a comment. \`cargo test\` and CI still run them.
test_broadband_single_source_doa_frequency_triples   # broadband_test, ~11 s
test_single_source_doa_noisy_10db                    # noisy_data_test, ~20 s
test_single_source_doa_noisy_5db                     # noisy_data_test, ~20 s
test_single_source_doa_noisy_1db                     # noisy_data_test, ~20 s
test_single_source_doa                               # integration_test, ~18 s
`;
const settings = JSON.stringify({hooks:{Stop:[{hooks:[{type:"command",command:'"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/run-tests.sh',timeout:900}]}]}}, null, 2)+'\n';
await $`git switch -c feat/stop-hook-tests`;
await write('.claude/hooks/run-tests.sh', script);
await write('.claude/hooks/slow-tests.txt', slow);
await write('.claude/settings.json', settings);
await $`chmod +x .claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`;
// test: dirty tree -> runs; then unchanged -> fast exit
const env = {CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: '/home/orchid/projects/musicrs'};
await $`rm -rf target/.claude-hook`;
let s=Date.now(); const a = await $`echo '{}' | .claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`.env(env).nothrow(); const ta=(Date.now()-s)/1000;
// simulate code change: touch a file
await $`touch src/lib.rs`;
s=Date.now(); const b = await $`echo '{}' | .claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`.env(env).nothrow(); const tb=(Date.now()-s)/1000;
s=Date.now(); const c = await $`echo '{}' | .claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`.env(env).nothrow(); const tc=(Date.now()-s)/1000;
const log = await $`grep -E "test result" target/.claude-hook/last-run.log`.nothrow().text();
({a:[a.exitCode,ta,a.output], b:[b.exitCode,tb,b.output], c:[c.exitCode,tc], log})

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Overview

**musicrs** is a Rust port of the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone/antenna arrays. Based on R. O. Schmidt's 1986 algorithm and the Python pyMUSIC implementation.

## Commands

```bash
# Build
cargo build
cargo build --release

# Test
cargo test              # all tests (unit + integration)
cargo test --lib        # unit tests only
cargo test --test '*'   # integration tests only
cargo test --test golden_test   # parity with the original pyMUSIC spectra
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   # CI runs this and `cargo fmt --check`

# Documentation
cargo doc --open
```

## Architecture

```
src/
├── lib.rs      # Public API exports and crate-level docs
├── music.rs    # Core MUSIC algorithm (MusicEstimator, spectrum, DOA estimation)
└── stft.rs     # Signal processing (STFT, analytic signal via Hilbert transform)
tests/
├── common/mod.rs                # Shared WAV/filename/angle helpers
├── integration_test.rs          # Narrowband DOA on every WAV recording (±5°)
├── ifb_test.rs                  # IFB-MUSIC on the tone's bin (nfft 160), below Nyquist (±5°)
├── golden_test.rs               # Spectra vs. original pyMUSIC output in tests/golden/
├── broadband_test.rs            # IFB-MUSIC on composite multi-tone signals
├── noisy_data_test.rs           # Narrowband DOA with added white noise
├── golden/                      # pyMUSIC reference CSVs + generate_golden.py
└── data/single-source/*.wav     # 4-channel 24-bit 16kHz test recordings
```

**Key types:**
- `MusicEstimator` — main struct; configure antenna positions, angle search range/step, sample rate, and number of sources
- `MusicEstimator::estimate_doa_from_real()` — real-data entry point (analytic signal per channel, then `estimate_doa`), like pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles`
- `MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum()` — wideband variant; bin frequencies use the estimator's `sample_rate`, so tones above Nyquist cannot be recovered
- `analytic_signal()` — converts real signal to complex via Hilbert transform (FFT-based)
- `stft()` — Short-Time Fourier Transform with configurable window and overlap

**Core algorithm flow:**
1. Compute covariance matrix of complex multichannel input
2. Hermitian eigendecomposition (`faer`) → signal/noise subspace split
3. Compute MUSIC pseudo-spectrum using steering vectors
4. Peak detection → DOA estimates in radians

## Dependencies

| Crate | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `nalgebra` | Matrix types and linear algebra |
| `num-complex` | Complex number arithmetic |
| `rustfft` | FFT for STFT and Hilbert transform |
| `faer` | Numerically stable Hermitian eigendecomposition |
| `hound` (dev) | Reading WAV test fixtures |
| `approx` (dev) | Floating-point approximate equality in tests |

## Testing

Integration tests load WAV files from `tests/data/single-source/` and verify DOA estimates within **±5°** of the known ground truth. File naming convention:

```
single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav
```

Test data covers:
- Frequencies: 300 Hz – 9.1 kHz (in ~1.1 kHz steps)
- Angles: 0°, 40°, 80°, 120°, 160°
- Durations: 1 s and 2 s
- Array: Kinect 4-mic geometry

## Workflow

- Make changes on a branch, never directly on `main`:
  - `feat/<feature-name>` for new features
  - `fix/<bugfix-name>` for bug fixes
- Structure work in reasonably sized commits: each commit is one logical change that builds and passes tests on its own.

## Notes

- Rust edition 2024, MSRV follows current stable toolchain
- No `rustfmt.toml` or `clippy.toml` — use `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` defaults
- Golden files: `*.eigh.csv` (pyMUSIC with `np.linalg.eigh`) must match value-by-value; `*.eig.csv` (pyMUSIC as published) only by peak location, because `np.linalg.eig` returns a non-orthogonal noise basis on this near-noiseless data. Regenerate with the command in `tests/golden/generate_golden.py`.
- Sign convention: musicrs uses a non-conjugated analytic signal with an `exp(+j2πfτ)` steering vector; pyMUSIC conjugates the analytic signal and uses `exp(−j2πfτ)`. Equivalent below Nyquist. The above-Nyquist sign flip and the real steering vector at Nyquist are musicrs additions tuned to the test data.

I added a project hook that runs the tests whenever Claude finishes a turn that changed code. Following the new workflow rules, it's on a branch `feat/stop-hook-tests` in two commits: the CLAUDE.md workflow rules first, then the hook. Nothing is pushed.

**How it works**
- `.claude/settings.json` sets the hook to run each time Claude finishes a turn. It calls `.claude/hooks/run-tests.sh`.
- The script only runs `cargo test` if files under `src/`, `tests/`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` changed since the last passing run. Turns that only touch docs or config cost about 0.1 s.
- If tests fail, the last 80 lines of output go back to Claude and it keeps working on them. If Claude then stops again without changing any code, the hook lets it stop, so it can't get stuck in a loop.

**Skipping slow tests**
- `.claude/hooks/slow-tests.txt` lists test names to skip, one per line. It currently has the five tests that take over 10 s each: the three noisy-data tests, the integration test and the broadband frequency-triples test. With those skipped, a run takes about 17 s instead of about 72 s. Plain `cargo test` and CI still run everything.
- To turn the hook off completely, set `MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1` before starting Claude Code.

**What I tested:** I ran the script directly with sample inputs rather than through a live Claude Code session. It skipped when nothing had changed, ran after a code change, and returned the failure with the test output when I added a deliberately failing test. With the "already retried" flag set and no further changes, it let Claude stop. The off switch worked. The failing test file is deleted.

**Things to know:**
- Each run writes its state and full output to `target/.claude-hook/`, which is already gitignored.
- The first time the hook runs, if the code has no uncommitted changes, it assumes the committed code is already tested and skips.
- Change detection looks at file sizes and modification times, so switching branches can cause one extra test run.

I also added a line about the hook to the Workflow section of CLAUDE.md. Do you want me to push the branch and open a PR?
well doesn't provide rust some mechnism to tag tests? so you can use a flag to exclude "slow" tagged tests
You're right. Rust's built-in way to do this is `#[ignore = "reason"]`. I'll switch to that.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code Stop hook: run the test suite when Claude finishes a turn that
# changed code (src/, tests/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock).
#
# Skipping:
#   - Slow tests carry #[ignore = "slow"]; plain `cargo test` (what this hook
#     runs) skips them. Run them with `cargo test -- --include-ignored`.
#   - MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1 in the environment Claude Code was started
#     from disables the hook entirely.
#
# Exit 2 with the failure output on stderr makes Claude keep working on it.
set -uo pipefail

input=$(cat)
[[ "${MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 0

cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(dirname "$0")/../..}" || exit 0

stamp_dir=target/.claude-hook
mkdir -p "$stamp_dir"
paths=(src tests Cargo.toml Cargo.lock)

# Cheap fingerprint of the code: name, size and mtime of every tracked or
# untracked (non-ignored) file under the code paths.
fingerprint=$(git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- "${paths[@]}" \
  | xargs -r -d '\n' stat -c '%n %s %Y' 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)

# Nothing changed since the last passing run.
[[ -f "$stamp_dir/passed" && "$(cat "$stamp_dir/passed")" == "$fingerprint" ]] && exit 0

# First run on a clean tree: assume the committed code is tested.
if [[ ! -f "$stamp_dir/passed" && -z "$(git status --porcelain -- "${paths[@]}")" ]]; then
  echo "$fingerprint" > "$stamp_dir/passed"
  exit 0
fi

# Claude already saw these failures and stopped without changing code: let it
# stop instead of looping.

content.text:
Yes. Rust's test runner has no general tags, but it has one built-in marker for this: `#[ignore = "reason"]`. I've switched the hook to use it and removed the separate skip-list file.

**What changed:**
- **Tests:** the five slow tests (the integration test, the three noisy-data tests and the broadband frequency-triples test) are now marked `#[ignore = "slow"]`.
- **Hook:** it now just runs plain `cargo test`, which leaves out tests marked this way. That takes about 12 s instead of about 72 s for everything.
- **Full suite:** `cargo test -- --include-ignored` runs everything. I ran it and all 42 tests pass.
- **CI:** CI now passes `--run-ignored all` to nextest, so pull requests still run the slow tests. nextest isn't installed here, so I couldn't try that change; the first CI run on a PR will confirm it.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the command list and the hook description are updated. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` pass.
- **Off switch:** `MUSICRS_SKIP_HOOK_TESTS=1` still turns the hook off completely.

**Tradeoff:** plain `cargo test` now skips the slow tests for you too, not just for the hook. That's why the full-suite command is in CLAUDE.md.

**Other options:**
- If you later want more than one category, Rust can't tell different ignore reasons apart. You'd need a naming prefix like `slow_`, filtered with `cargo test -- --skip slow_`, or nextest's filter expressions.
- If you'd rather keep plain `cargo test` running everything, the alternative is `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "slow-tests"), ignore)]` with a Cargo feature. It's wordier.
